item.title: Visegrád Four leaders voice concerns over EU budget proposal
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said his government did not consider the proposal an acceptable starting point for negotiations.

item.title: Tanzania: Towering flames engulf beachfront hotels in Zanzibar
item.description: A massive fire swept through six beachfront hotels on the island of Zanzibar, Tanzania, on Saturday 21 November 2026, forcing around 180 tourists to evacuate as flames spread rapidly along the popular Nungwi Beach.

item.title: German-Ukrainian interceptor shoots down Russian jet-powered drone, company says
item.description: The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 drone in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.

item.title: Belgium: Workers march against spending cuts as living costs rise
item.description: Thousands marched through Brussels, on Monday 23 November 2026, against proposed austerity measures, with some clashes prompting police to deploy tear gas and water cannons. The protests came as Belgium's government struggled to agree on its budget for 2027.

item.title: What went wrong at the COP31 climate talks? Europe Tonight breaks it down
item.description: Euronews' Felicia Pochhammer spoke to Chiara Martinelli, the director of Climate Action Network, to look at what went wrong at the COP31 climate talks and what it means for Europe and for the future of global climate action.

item.title: NATO warns of intensifying threats as Ukraine peace proposals face key questions
item.description: Henri Vanhanen, a senior fellow with the Transatlantic Security Initiative, joined Euronews’ new show Europe Tonight to discuss growing security concerns and the prospects for peace in Ukraine.

item.title: Merz says it was a 'mistake' not to admit Ukraine into NATO in 2008
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters the Russian invasion of Ukraine would likely not have happened if allies had agreed to admit Kyiv in 2008 during a summit in Bucharest.

item.title: 'Don't waste those talents': GTA VI hacker released on licence
item.description: Arion Kurtaj managed to obtain 90 gameplay videos from Rockstar's much anticipated and at the time unfinished GTA VI game before leaking them online under the pseudonym "TeaPotUberHacker."

item.title: Iran carries out flogging of singer who performed without hijab
item.description: Ahmadi and four members of her concert team received lashes in Qom on Monday, her lawyer said, over a December 2024 performance, streamed live without an audience. A court sentenced nine team members to 74 lashes each, a two-year travel ban, and a two-year ban on artistic activity.

item.title: No, Greenland isn't being handed over to Trump. But what exactly has Washington secured?
item.description: The agreement builds on a 1951 defence agreement and comes after months of heightened tensions between Washington and the island under Danish sovereignty.

item.title: United Kingdom to host 2035 Women's World Cup, FIFA confirms
item.description: The chief executives of the English, Northern Irish, Scottish and Welsh football associations released a joint statement on Monday calling it a "landmark moment."

item.title: Von der Leyen and Kushner clash over peace talks sequence
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen and Jared Kushner cannot agree on when and how the issue of European security archicture should be discussed in the peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 23rd, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 23rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Europe Tonight: NATO security warnings, COP31 fallout, and Spain’s elections
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte warns of escalating hybrid threats as Ukraine pushes for membership, COP31 collapses without a climate deal, Spain faces a pivotal right-wing electoral shift, IG Metall workers strike across Germany, and Paris illuminates the Champs-Élysées for the holidays.

item.title: How artists from Qatar, Canada and Mexico are connecting cultures through creativity
item.description: Artists from Qatar, Mexico and Canada explore shared traditions, personal histories and new creative connections through the 2026 Year of Culture.

item.title: Dutch court bans BYD model from EU over likeness to Land Rover's Defender
item.description: The Chinese carmaker plans to appeal, and the ruling doesn't stop the car going on sale in Britain in January.

item.title: Macron announces €350 million research aid for France's aeronautics industry
item.description: During a visit to the Airbus site in Blagnac near Toulouse, the French president announced 350 million euros in state support for aeronautics research and innovation, plus special industrial zones to ease new factory projects.

item.title: AI just cracked the biggest maths problem of all time: what does it mean?
item.description: Some wonder if the solving of the famous Riemann Hypothesis by Anthropic’s Claude model is the beginning of advanced super intelligence.

item.title: EU goes after Russia's banks, soldiers and athletes in new sanctions package
item.description: Russian banks, crypto, "shadow fleet", oil refineries, soldiers and athletes are all targeted in the latest sanctions package proposed by Brussels.

item.title: Finland summons Russian ambassador as it condemns Russia's 'dangerous and reckless actions' in Europe
item.description: It comes after a Russian helicopter was suspected of having violated Finnish airspace on Saturday afternoon, off the coast of Loviisa.

item.title: Ukraine releases footage of strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya
item.description: Ukraine has released footage showing what it says are strikes against two Russian vessels off the Libyan port of Benghazi.

item.title: How Iceland's Blue Lagoon is faring after its long-awaited stock market debut
item.description: Shares in Iceland's Blue Lagoon fell below their offer price when they started trading on Friday. The geothermal spa operator raised 14.3 billion Icelandic krónur (€104mn) in the country's first IPO in nearly three years.

item.title: 'Return the Marbles': Greece renews demand for Parthenon relics at Acropolis Museum reopening
item.description: "The place of these priceless masterpieces is here, under the Attic light and in direct contact with the temple they belong to," said Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis.

item.title: South Korea’s education minister resigns after backlash over AI exam cheating rules
item.description: South Korea’s university entrance exam can shape a student’s future. Hidden cameras and smart glasses have fuelled fears of AI-assisted cheating, prompting last-minute security measures that drew criticism and led to the education minister’s resignation.

item.title: ‘Batman Returns’: Tim Burton’s iconic Batmobile car heads to auction
item.description: The iconic Batmobile from Tim Burton’s 1992 film Batman Returns is heading to auction with an estimated price of $5 million to $7 million.

item.title: Robotaxis and stock exchanges: Why Bolt's CEO says Europe is way behind
item.description: Bolt’s CEO spoke to Euronews about the company’s future IPO plans, why he believes Europe is falling behind, and whether the US could offer a more attractive market. He also shared his vision for the future of autonomous vehicles.

item.title: At least 24 people killed in Indonesia factory fire, police say
item.description: Dozens of employees are still reported to be missing after a blaze broke out at a candy factory in Banten province at around 4:30 pm local time on Saturday.

item.title: Nvidia closes up more than 30% after Jensen Huang returns as CEO
item.description: Nvidia shares soared from their Friday close after the company's board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. US President Donald Trump welcomed his return.

item.title: Portishead join ‘No Music For Genocide’ campaign alongside Massive Attack, Fontaines D.C. and Björk
item.description: Iconic trip-hop band Portishead has joined the ‘No Music For Genocide’ campaign, a cultural boycott initiative encouraging artists and rights-holders to pull their music from streaming platforms in Israel.

item.title: How a winemaker found his home and his market in Macao
item.description: From Portuguese heritage and independent restaurants to luxury resorts and quiet hilltop runs, winemaker Eddie McDougall explains how Macao shaped both his career and his life since he moved there for his wife’s work.

item.title: China: 5,000 drones illuminate sky over Three Gorges at autumn festival
item.description: Five thousand drones lit up the night sky over Wushan, southwest China, creating giant images of autumn leaves, mountains and river landscapes. The spectacular display celebrated the region's annual Red Leaf Festival.

item.title: LEGO to build €1bn factory in Portugal, creating more than 1,000 jobs
item.description: The Danish toymaker plans to invest around €1 billion over several years in its fourth European factory. LEGO says the plant will be its most technologically advanced and is expected to start production in 2030.

item.title: Croatia steps up pressure on Montenegro over border dispute as EU accession deadline looms
item.description: Zagreb is demanding a settlement over a strategically important peninsula as Montenegro races to conclude its EU accession talks by the end of the year, raising fears that the dispute could derail its membership ambitions.

item.title: South Korea and China agree wider trade deal covering entertainment
item.description: South Korean entertainment companies have faced barriers in China since a dispute over a US missile defence system in 2016. New trade commitments could improve access, but content checks on films remain and a return of K-pop concerts is not guaranteed.

item.title: Japan launches Asian oil task force amid Gulf supply disruptions
item.description: Disruptions to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran war have pushed Asian countries to look at larger emergency reserves, shared storage, and closer cooperation with fuel suppliers as shortages squeeze their economies.

item.title: Hungary's PM to visit Transcarpathia, pledges support to Ukrainian people and local Hungarians
item.description: Ties soured sharply under Hungary's previous PM Viktor Orbán, whose government repeatedly clashed with Kyiv over Ukraine and blocked its progress towards EU membership.

item.title: CrowdStrike buys Zscaler in €40 billion cybersecurity deal
item.description: The merging of the two companies is one of the biggest cybersecurity deals in history.

item.title: EU opens antitrust probe into Coca-Cola's European distributor
item.description: Discounts that depended on drinks staying inside national borders, and a refusal to sign supermarket deals covering more than one country, are among the practices under scrutiny.

item.title: Mercedes, BMW hit by 24-hour strikes as German pay dispute widens
item.description: IG Metall, Germany’s largest trade union, called on more than 23,000 workers at 19 northern sites to join a 24-hour strike. The walkouts hit Mercedes-Benz, BMW, and Siemens Gamesa, with Meyer Werft workers also called out.

item.title: Exclusive: China-backed hackers suspected behind ongoing EU Commission cyberattack
item.description: The European Commission suspects a China-backed hacking group is behind a cyberattack that has hit its systems for a month and is still ongoing. The first confirmed leak of personal data involves EU Academy users.

item.title: EU military chief warns of escalating hybrid threats as Europe races to strengthen defences
item.description: General Seán Clancy says Europe is better prepared to defend itself but must speed up efforts to close critical military gaps, amid growing threats from Russia and uncertainty over US military commitments.

item.title: Donald Trump urges Nvidia to rehire former CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: US President Donald Trump has urged Nvidia's board to rehire Jensen Huang, joining calls for his return that include a petition with more than 200,000 signatures. The former CEO is due to face questions in Congress on 1 December.

item.title: Iran vows 'every means' to counter US blockade of Hormuz after Trump threat
item.description: Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the blockade an "act of crime" a day after Trump said Iranian ships trying to break it would go "to the bottom of the sea".

item.title: Bomb threats emailed to German schools present no 'concrete danger,' police say
item.description: It comes after more than 300 schools across Italy were evacuated earlier this month after receiving emailed bomb threats, which also claimed that an explosive device had been planted in Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s car.

item.title: Can AI help detect breast cancer faster? Major new trial will find out
item.description: Researchers will test whether an AI tool helps radiologists detect breast cancer.

item.title: 'We should not be okay with a handover of society to AI', warns Meta's AI boss
item.description: Alexandr Wang has raised concerns over the latest achievements of AI and the risk posed by super intelligent AI models to humanity.

item.title: From COP31 Antalya to Copenhagen: UN climate summits where no agreement was reached
item.description: Since 1995, UN climate and environment summits have often seen deadlock, delays and frustration.

item.title: Eight EU countries join forces to defend carbon market against calls for delay
item.description: The eight countries warn that further delays to the EU's expanded carbon market would undermine energy security, prolong dependence on fossil fuel imports and jeopardise investment in clean technologies.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 23rd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 23rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Belgian unions lead protest against austerity policies as government's future hangs in balance
item.description: Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation to the king on 2 November over the budget impasse, but the monarch refused to accept it and gave him more time to find a solution.
